**Conversation overview**

This conversation is a continuation of an ongoing long-form editorial and computational project called "The Method 1.6," operating under a structured session protocol called the Prime Handoff Directive and Prime Zeno Directive. The person is the author of a multi-volume scholarly work comprising a main volume, Register, Mathematical Compendium, Physics Compendium, Index of Indices, and Spectra Compendium, plus associated instruments (Python scripts). Each chat session follows a strict reading gate (§0) before any work begins, producing a certificate of measured file state. The session was chat 25, operating on BUILD-25 bundles and producing BUILD-26. The project maintains a WORKING-REGISTER.md of rulings and work notes, and a formal Register of numbered entries (165–1773 at close).

The session closed two standing questions from a list carried since HANDOFF-22 §5B. IOI-09 concerned a 98.6% ceiling on measurable spectral cells in the Index of Indices: Claude read the enclosing section, located Register entries 983 and 984, and computed that the printed ceiling was wrong — it used 18 (the fixable kind) rather than 14 (the unfixable kind) as the numerator of unreachable cells, giving 98.6% instead of the correct 98.9%. Claude also identified that the paragraph fused three kinds of unreachable cells into two clauses. The author authorised correction to 98.9% with the three kinds split out and Register entry 1771 written. SPEC-01 concerned a section heading "The bounds on the unwitnessed" in the Spectra Compendium that was falsified by 25 witnessed cells also carrying bounds. The author rejected Claude's initial proposal as over-complicated, and after two short exchanges settled on the heading "The bounds, witnessed and unwitnessed." Register entry 1772 was written and two Spectra sites updated without moving the table. The author also directed that four citation figures in the Register's front matter (392/713/968 and 556) be restated to current values (386/699/966 and 565), with the editorial process remark struck — this became Ruling 45, which also establishes a general prohibition on build or editorial-process remarks in any volume, to be executed via a 27-site list put to the author before sweeping. Register entry 1773 records the restatement. Two rulings received verbatim from the author resolved previously open questions: Ruling 43 (editorial volume changes go to the working register only, never the books, unblocking Ruling 42's execution) and Ruling 44 (the complete transition table goes into the Index of Indices as its own section, entered by a new Register entry citing 1770, with 1770 untouched).

The author twice corrected Claude's approach to standing questions: once for over-complicating IOI-09's framing before having the materials in hand, and once for over-complicating SPEC-01 by treating a straightforward heading question as a multi-part arithmetic problem. The author's correction on SPEC-01 was that the table simply has witnessed and unwitnessed values, the latter being theoretical predictions supported by the witnessed values that make up the Löwdin solution. The author's correction on the citation figures was that dated readings still need to be restated — dating a figure makes it defensible, not current, and a reader wants the current number. The standing lesson added to HANDOFF-27 is: put the materials in front of the author with the question, keep the question to three sentences, and let the arithmetic decide before asking. BUILD-26 was packed (88 members, two bundles, zero mismatches on byte-identical round-trip) and HANDOFF-27 written. Nine standing questions (items 6–14) remain open for chat 26, along with the press on four volumes, Ruling 42's and Ruling 45's site-list sweeps, the reader reads (A4, A5, A6), and Ruling 44's build.

**Tool knowledge**

Claude used bash extensively for file measurement and editing throughout. The reliable pattern for guarding single-site edits is `assert t.count(anchor)==1` before any `.replace()` — this caught zero cases of multi-site contamination this session but is the standing discipline. For citation recomputation, the critical lesson recorded in G7 is that reimplementing `register_cites.py`'s parser inline produces wrong results (239/

**The main volume has no corresponding section.** Measured: `Λ_spectra` appears in the main volume exactly **once**, at line 10847, inside a table row making a different claim (`Λ_spectra closes at the last species, E = 11`). No `98.6`, no `1,312`, no channel survey, no unconstrained cells. The ceiling claim lives in the Index of Indices alone, at line 308, and nowhere else in any volume.

**The section it sits in — IoI "The channel survey — Λ_spectra^obs" (lines 277–310)** — builds to it through a grade table:

| grade | cells |
|---|---|
| MEASURED | 205 |
| BRACKETED | 5 |
| BOUNDED | 42 |
| PROPAGATED | 954 |
| FORMAL | 73 |
| UNCONSTRAINED | **33** |

Those sum to **1,312**, and 1,312 is the denominator the whole section uses. It checks out twice: (1,312−33)/1,312 = **97.48%**, the section's printed 97.5%; and R981's earlier 96.9% is (1,312−41)/1,312 = 96.88%. The denominator is sound.

**Register 984 is the source, and it accounts for all 33 exactly** — the IoI prose compresses it:

- **Ar I** — one cell at d, an ordinary gap → **1**
- **P I, Cd I, Ti II** — six each at ℓ ≥ 2, wanting a longer capture → **18**
- **Sc I and Ti I** — no Rydberg series to capture → **14**

1 + 18 + 14 = 33. R984's own words: *the last of those is not a queue item.*

**So the arithmetic decides more than I said it could.** Fourteen is the unfixable kind, confirmed by R983 and R984 and by the IoI's own sentence *only two of which a capture can fix*. Ceiling = (1,312−14)/1,312 = **98.93%**. And 98.6% is exactly (1,312−**18**)/1,312 — 18 being the count of the *P I / Cd I / Ti II* group, the kind that **is** fixable. The printed ceiling was computed off the wrong one of the three kinds.

**My earlier inference is refuted and I'm withdrawing it.** IOI-09 guessed a hidden fourth-cell group making 18; R984 shows there is none. Marked as refuted-by-record, not carried forward.

**And the third kind is not missing — it is fused.** The IoI sentence gives two clauses for three kinds: *"P I, Cd I, Ti II and Ar I want longer captures"* merges Ar I's single ordinary gap with the six-each trio. All four cell counts — 1, 18, 14, 33 — are in R984 and absent from the printed prose.

content.text:
**Segment D closed. The work is built.**

**Three volumes changed — main, Register, Index of Indices — and Register entry 1771 records all three in the same build.** No silent change. Verified by md5 against a pristine re-split of BUILD-25: the Mathematical, Physics and Spectra compendia are byte-identical and untouched.

What moved, all measured:

- **IoI line 308** — the one site in any volume carrying the claim. Ceiling 98.6% → **98.9%**, with `(1,312 − 14) / 1,312` printed beside it so a reader can reproduce it. The fused clause split into Ar I's one, the trio's eighteen, Sc I and Ti I's fourteen, and the sentence *One, eighteen and fourteen make the 33* added so the accounting closes on the page. Now cites **983 and 984**; it cited only 983 before.
- **Register 1771** appended — a correction, carrying both states, naming 98.6% as `(1,312 − 18)/1,312` and why eighteen was the wrong kind.
- **Counts to fixed point** — 1,450 headings, 1,475 numbers, 165–1771; both Register count lines; both main prose sentences; `kinds.py --write` moved corrections 128 → 129 and re-ran byte-identical.
- **My earlier inference withdrawn on the record.** IOI-09 guessed a hidden fourth group of four unfixable cells to make 18. R984 refutes it. It was marked inferred rather than measured, which is the only reason it didn't harden into a fact.

**Two things held, not repaired.** The Register's front matter prints 392 / 713 / 968 citation figures *"recomputed at Build 15"*, and the load-bearing section prints 556; the instrument returns 390 / 708 / 979 and 569. They are **dated readings, so they are not false**, and restating them is your ruling, not mine. My edit moved two of them by exactly one, and the cause is single and nameable: **entry 984 had never been cited by anything, by any volume, until 1771 cited it.**

**The press is now owed** — chat 24's pressed objects are stale on three volumes. Not run this segment.

---

Ten questions remain. Bringing the materials with the next one, since that is what the last one needed.
